chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from al-Zurari, who said:

I went with Bukayr and a man from the descendants of Ali to the sacred sites until we reached Uhud. He showed us the graves of the martyrs, then led us into the valley. We walked with him for a while until we arrived at a mosque there. He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed here,' so we prayed there. Then he showed us a place at the top of a mountain and said: 'The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) climbed to it, and rainwater would be there.'

Al-Zurari said: It occurred to me that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would not have climbed to fetch water there. So I said: 'I will not go with you; I will sleep here until you return.' He and Bukayr went, then they returned to me, and we all returned together.

The next day, we visited Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and he asked us: 'Where were you yesterday? I did not see you.' We informed him and described to him the mosque and the place where it was claimed the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) climbed. He washed his face there.

Abu Ja'far said: 'The Messenger of Allah never went to that place.' We said to him: 'It has been narrated to us that his tooth was broken.' He replied: 'No, Allah took him back whole, but his face was injured. He sent Ali, who brought him water in a shield. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) refused to drink from it, but washed his face.'

key_terms.الرَّبَاعِيَة: The canine tooth (specifically referring to the Prophet's tooth)
key_terms.حُجْفَة: A shield or a hollowed-out piece of wood used as a vessel
key_terms.شُجَّ: To be injured or wounded (specifically facial injury)
key_terms.قَبَضَهُ اللَّهُ سَلِيمًا: Allah took him back whole (referring to the Prophet's physical integrity)

ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet Muhammad climb a mountain to fetch water at Uhud according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* highlights the critical role of the Imams in verifying historical narratives against popular misconceptions, specifically correcting the belief that the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) ascended a mountain for rainwater. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the Prophet was physically intact at his death, with the injury being limited to his face, and Ali (AS) facilitated his ablution using a shield, emphasizing the purity and completeness of his physical state. This narration serves as a key example of *islah al-akhbar* (correction of traditions) within Shia scholarship, distinguishing between literal historical events and later accretions.

en.basel-kadem: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad b. Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said:

I went with Bukayr and a man from the descendants of Ali to the sacred sites until we reached Uhud. He showed us the graves of the martyrs, then led us into the valley. We walked with him for a while until we arrived at a mosque, where he said: "The Messenger of Allah (saw) prayed here," so we prayed there. Then he showed us a place at the top of a mountain and said: "The Prophet (saw) climbed this and found rainwater here."

Zurara said: It occurred to me that the Messenger of Allah (saw) would not have climbed to fetch water. So I said: "I will not continue with you. I will sleep here until you return." He and Bukayr went and then came back to me, and we all returned together.

The next day, we visited Abu Ja'far (as), who asked us: "Where were you yesterday? I did not see you." We informed him and described to him the mosque and the place where it was claimed the Prophet (saw) had climbed and washed his face.

Abu Ja'far said: "The Messenger of Allah (saw) never went to that place." 

We then said: "It has been narrated to us that his tooth was broken." He replied: "No, Allah took him back whole, but his face was injured. He sent Ali, who brought water in a shield, but the Messenger of Allah (saw) refused to drink from it and only washed his face."
